note: Declarations a migration makes that a freshly provisioned database does not have. A migration at or below BASELINE_CUTOFF = 219 is MARKED, never run, by `migrate-d1 --bootstrap`, so its effect reaches a database only if schema_baseline.sql already carries it — and the baseline is a dump of production, so what is listed here is absent from production too, while the ledger row says the migration was applied. The gate fails on NEW entries, and also on entries here whose declaration a fresh build has since gained, so this list cannot go stale. Three key shapes: `table:<name>` for a declared table the build lacks, `<table>.<column>` for a column declared on a table the build has, and `alter-orphan:<table>.<column>` for an ALTER … ADD COLUMN whose table exists nowhere at all. Every entry below was checked individually against a fresh build and, where it has a reader, against production studioos-db read-only on 2026-09-21. Re-measured read-only against production on 2026-09-22 for D190: migration 278 closes seven of these (the six tables 034/048/056/114 declare and 095's partners.accepting_intros), and two more — table:referral_attributions and table:admin_publications — were found to self-heal through a D95 runtime bootstrap, so their reasons were corrected rather than their gaps closed. AN ENTRY HERE MEANS A FRESH BUILD LACKS THE DECLARATION. It does NOT mean the reader is broken: check for a runtime CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS before writing a behavioural claim into a reason, because reading this guard's finding as behaviour is how four wrong reasons reached this file.
resolve_with: npx --no-install wrangler d1 execute studioos-db --remote --config ../wrangler.toml --env production --command "SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info('<table>')"

declarations.table:admin_publications: 045_admin_publications.sql. LIVE READERS: services/publications.ts:504 and routes/admin_publications.ts:93,178. CORRECTED 2026-09-22 (D190): this entry first said "every one of those statements answers `no such table` in production" and that "giving it a store is a product decision about whether that surface is still wanted". BOTH ARE FALSE — the table SELF-HEALS at runtime. ensureSchema (routes/admin_publications.ts:36) is a D95 WeakMap/bindingKey bootstrap around CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, awaited by all six handlers (:150, :200, :216, :253, :307, :420). The one path that looked like a hole is closed: services/publications.ts:500's uniqueSlug has exactly one caller, admin_publications.ts:436, and it sits inside the /publish handler that awaits ensureSchema sixteen lines earlier. Same mistake as its sibling above — the guard's finding is about a fresh build, not about behaviour — so the entry STAYS and no product decision is owed. Measured read-only against production on 2026-09-22: sqlite_master holds NEITHER this table NOR its counterpart above, so neither bootstrap has yet run there — absent today, created by the first reader to arrive, which is a different claim from broken. D190 therefore leaves it to its bootstrap rather than restoring it in migration 278.
declarations.table:referral_attributions: 100_referral_attributions.sql. LIVE READERS: services/referralAttribution.ts:72,82,108 (INSERT OR IGNORE, SELECT and UPDATE). CORRECTED 2026-09-22 (D190): this entry first said "Referral attribution therefore records nothing, which is money-adjacent and deserves its own PR". THAT IS FALSE — the table SELF-HEALS at runtime. ensureAttributionSchema (:23) is a D95 WeakMap/bindingKey bootstrap around CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, and BOTH public entry points await it as their first statement: captureAndResolveAttribution (:61) and markAttributionConverted (:106). The module's only other export, readRefCookie (:118), parses a cookie header and touches no database. Unlike D189's ALTERs — dead on arrival against D1's 100-column cap on `users` — a CREATE TABLE has no limit to hit, so the bootstrap succeeds the first time a reader arrives. The mistake was reading this guard's finding as a behavioural claim: the guard is right that a FRESH BUILD lacks the table (nothing above the cutoff creates it), which is why the entry STAYS, but a fresh build lacking it says nothing about whether a runtime bootstrap heals it. Measured read-only against production on 2026-09-22: sqlite_master holds NEITHER this table NOR its counterpart above, so neither bootstrap has yet run there — absent today, created by the first reader to arrive, which is a different claim from broken. D190 therefore leaves it to its bootstrap rather than restoring it in migration 278.

declarations.users.google_sub: 061_google_sub.sql. GENUINELY SUPERSEDED, not a gap: the live reader is user_google_links.google_sub (routes/settings.ts:1848, services/fundSheets.ts:283,290), a different table that exists and holds 22 linked accounts. Nothing reads users.google_sub.
declarations.users.marketing_unsubscribed_at: 053_notifications_center.sql. routes/notifications.ts:51 lazily runs `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN marketing_unsubscribed_at` at runtime inside `catch { /* idempotent */ }`. CORRECTED: this entry first said the column 'self-heals the first time that route is hit — and production not having it means that route has never once been hit'. BOTH HALVES ARE FALSE. AND THE ALTER CAN NEVER SUCCEED, which the first draft of this entry missed: `users` sits at D1's hard 100-column cap — measured 2026-09-21, production `pragma_table_info('users')` = 100, and a fresh build the same. cloudflare-worker/src/util/schemaBootstrap.ts's header records the same fact against production on 2026-09-04, and migration 199 hit it for real on 2026-09-03 (#413), holding 200-207 out of production behind it. So this is NOT a gap to close with another ADD COLUMN — the deploy would fail and every later migration would be stranded. It needs a side table keyed by user_id, on the `super_admins` precedent (199, D35), which is what D189 built. Because the lazy ALTER cannot succeed, the column never self-heals, and its absence says nothing about whether the route was hit. The UPDATE on the next line then fails too, swallowed by applyMarketingUnsub's outer catch — so an unsubscribe from marketing email silently records nothing, which is compliance-adjacent rather than cosmetic. services/email/send.ts:117 reads it inside a try, so marketing suppression fails open. CORRECTED 2026-09-22 (D190): the paragraph above is the state BEFORE D189, which merged as e291a437d on 2026-09-22 and is deployed. Migration 277 created the side tables `user_recovery_state` and `user_marketing_prefs`, verified present in production with their declared shapes, and every reader was repointed: auth.ts:369-372 hydrates recovery_cooling_off_until / recovery_step_up_due_at onto the user object FROM the side table, so middleware/recoveryCoolOff.ts:20 and auth.ts:453 read a hydrated field rather than a column, and routes/notifications.ts:51 records that its lazy ALTER "used to run". So the 500s and the silent unsubscribe are FIXED and this entry no longer describes live behaviour. It is PERMANENT rather than pending: `users` is still at the cap, the column is still absent from a fresh build by design, and the guard is right to keep listing a declaration the build does not have. Delete it only if `users` is ever rebuilt below the cap.

declarations.users.advisor_extras_json: 042_advisor_field_sources.sql:70 declares it and the ALTER CAN NEVER SUCCEED on D1: D1 caps a table at 100 columns and `users` is at exactly 100 — measured read-only against production on 2026-09-21, `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_table_info('users')` = 100. Migration 199 hit this for real on 2026-09-03 (#413): its `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN` failed with "too many columns on sqlite_altertab_users" and, because the runner is forward-only and ordered, held 200-207 out of production behind it. So this is not a gap to close with a twelfth ADD COLUMN — the fact lives in the side table `user_advisor_extras`, created by 276_advisor_field_sources_remainder.sql on the `super_admins` precedent (199, D35), and services/advisor/writeRouter.ts's mergeUserExtras and hydrateAlreadyAnswered read it there. Delete this entry only if `users` is ever rebuilt below the cap; until then it is one of FOUR declarations in this ledger that are dead by a platform limit rather than by an accident, not the only one: the other three are users.recovery_cooling_off_until and users.recovery_step_up_due_at (060) and users.marketing_unsubscribed_at (053), each on the same full table. CORRECTED: this entry, and PR #705's body, first called it 'the one'. node:sqlite has no such cap, which is why a fresh local build applies 042's ALTER happily and only frontend/test/migration_column_shapes.test.mjs can see it.
